extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and descriptive norms for using the MathOverflow Q&A site: what kinds of questions are appropriate, formatting expectations for mathematics, community scope, and behavior norms. Targeted at prospective contributors and readers of MathOverflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary purpose / scope
rubrics_metrics.description: It is primarily for asking questions on mathematics research – i.e. related to unsolved problems and the extension of knowledge of mathematics into areas that are not yet known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the site for research-level mathematical questions rather than instructional or elementary homework-style problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience / community
rubrics_metrics.description: MathOverflow serves as an online community of mathematicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributions should be aimed at a mathematically sophisticated audience (professional mathematicians, researchers, advanced students).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable topics beyond research questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The site does welcome various questions on other topics that might normally be discussed among mathematicians, for example about publishing, refereeing, advising, getting tenure, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-technical matters related to the professional practice of mathematics (publishing, refereeing, career advice) are permitted when appropriate and framed for the mathematical community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disallowed / discouraged content
rubrics_metrics.description: It does not welcome requests from non-mathematicians for instruction, for example homework exercises. It is generally inhospitable to questions perceived as tendentious or argumentative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid posting homework-style requests seeking instruction for non-research purposes, and avoid tendentious/argumentative formats; questions should be neutral, focused, and research-oriented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of mathematical formulas and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: To support most of the functionality of LaTeX, MathJax was added so that any post including 'Math Mode' (text between $s) will translate into proper mathematical notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write mathematical content using MathJax/LaTeX syntax (enclose inline math with $...$) to ensure correct rendering; this is the supported way to include formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming / site branding
rubrics_metrics.description: According to MathOverflow FAQ, the proper spelling is 'MathOverflow' rather than 'Math Overflow'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the canonical site name 'MathOverflow' in references and branding.

rubrics_metrics.name: User actions and reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: The site allows users to ask questions, submit answers, and rate both, all while getting merit points for their activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participate by asking, answering, and voting; reputation/merit points accrue based on these activities and are part of the site's incentive structure.
